name: Lake Lanier
headline: The lake behind Atlanta's taps
story: Lake Lanier anchors metro Atlanta's water supply. Alabama sued in 1990 and Florida joined;[[arc-wars]] in 2021 the Supreme Court unanimously rejected Florida's case.[[scotus-2021]]
done: In 2024 the Army Corps adopted a Georgia–Alabama deal to settle the dispute.[[arc-2025]]

stat.label: gallons a day for metro Atlanta through 2050

whyYou: The water in your campus tap starts here.

name: Midtown, near campus
headline: When century-old pipes burst
story: On May 31, 2024, pipes the mayor dated to 1910 and 1930 broke, one under a mile from Tech Tower.[[cnn-2024]] Downtown and Midtown lost safe tap water.[[ap-2024]]
done: The Army Corps came to help assess the aging pipes.[[cnn-2024]]

stat.label: until the last boil-water advisory lifted

whyYou: It happened a short walk from Tech Square.

image.alt: Midtown Atlanta near the Georgia Tech campus.

name: Proctor Creek, Westside
headline: Still failing bacteria standards
story: It flows nine miles from near downtown to the Chattahoochee.[[epa-proctor]] It's listed as impaired for E. coli;[[epd-303d-2024]] EPA says high levels can signal leaking sewers.[[epa-proctor]]
done: Sewer repairs and planned green infrastructure should help clean it up.[[epa-proctor]]

stat.label: typical E. coli vs. the state standard near downtown

whyYou: That river supplies Atlanta's tap water.

name: Rural Middle Georgia
headline: The septic tank out back
story: Septic systems that are aging or poorly maintained can fail and pollute waterways.[[uga-septic]] In part of Twiggs County, homes have no public sewer at all.[[epd-twiggs-2025]]
done: UGA researchers convened wastewater experts to work on fixes.[[uga-septic]]
whyYou: Engineers like you can design cheaper, better systems.

name: Savannah & Brunswick coast
headline: Salt seeping into the aquifer
story: The Upper Floridan aquifer is the coast's main water source. Heavy pumping lowered water levels and let saltwater in at Brunswick and Hilton Head, S.C.[[usgs-pubs-2001]]
done: No new wells are allowed near Brunswick's plume, and Savannah's pumping is capped.[[epd-coastal-2006]]

stat.label: coastal counties where Georgia manages pumping

whyYou: From the coast? This is likely your tap water.

image.alt: Salt marsh on the Georgia coast.

name: Albany & the Lower Flint
headline: Thirsty crops, shrinking streams
story: Farming uses over 70% of the region's water.[[asu-2022]] After a drought, Georgia froze new farm permits in 2012; well permits with drought limits reopened in 2025.[[gpb-2024]]
done: Now farms are switching to deep wells in droughts.[[asu-2022]]

stat.label: lower streamflow since 1975; up to half in La Niña growing seasons

whyYou: These farms and your tap share one river system.
